claim_under_test: The original R1 structural-inability diagnosis is withdrawn because the model can generate separated peaks; the withdrawal is then used to assert intact apparent-potential broadening physics.

facets.finding: At 298.15 K the shipped n=1 configuration has one local maximum while setting every transition to n=0.12 gives four.
All four graphite transitions still ship with n=1; no default was changed to the narrow demonstration value.
The code exposes n or w as fit handles, but n takes precedence and the four stored w fallbacks are inert under shipped defaults.
The manuscript distinguishes a two-phase near-delta equilibrium response from apparent-potential broadening and writes a forward ensemble average.
One paragraph says finite-current contribution 1 is excluded from w and handled by L_V, while the later keybox says all three sources are absorbed by the phenomenological width.
The theory writes an explicit rho(U_app) forward ensemble integral, while production implements one effective logistic width and no explicit ensemble distribution or convolution.
The v1.0.12 sample honestly labels default n=1 as merged and fitted n=0.12 as four resolved peaks.
The stored v1.0.12 PNG and generator were committed together and visual review confirms the labeled comparison.
The copied v1.0.12 regression script still hardcodes the v1.0.10 production path, has no Python assert and does not gate peak count or two-phase provenance.
The sample counts peaks but explicitly calls the output report-only and never fails when the peak count or physical interpretation is wrong.
No source, test or figure in this lineage fits a public graphite data set to discriminate equilibrium, heterogeneity, kinetic and instrument widths.
Unconstrained inverse PSD recovery should remain prohibited, but a blanket ban on separating equilibrium, kinetics, heterogeneity and observation layers is scientifically unsupported.
